event.description: Frances Loeb Library Faculty Author Talk Please join us in the library for a conversation between Hannah Ahlblad and Jorge Otero-Pailos on Treaties on De-Fences. Treaties on De-Fences is an artist book of prints created by Jorge Otero-Pailos and made available to the public on the occasion of his 2024 Park Avenue sculptures exhibition Analogue Sites. Much like the exhibition, the artist’s book of prints aims to raise awareness and advocate for the preservation of modernist U.S. embassies. While the art installation uses large sculptures, as a method to make these embassies visible and tangible to the general public, the artist's book of prints further enacts and intertwines the energy of the sculptures and the diplomatic treaties from which the sculptures derive their names. This event is free and open to the public. Participants are invited to attend in person in the Loeb Library or join via livestream, here. This event will be recorded.
event.title: Treaties on De-Fences

event.description: Amy Kyungwon Han (Associate Professor, Seoul National University) Soft robotics enables safe and adaptive interaction with humans, delicate objects, and dynamic environments through compliant actuators, sensors, and mechanisms. This talk presents the design and application of soft robotic technologies for haptics, gripping, and medical applications, with an emphasis on compact, low-power, and application-specific solutions. Examples include an origami-based haptic device for remote manipulation, hybrid electrostatic mechanisms for handling deformable objects with reduced gripping force, and soft cardiac assistive technologies designed to operate under physiological constraints. Through these examples, the talk highlights how mechanism design and system integration can address challenges in actuation, sensing, safety, and compatibility, demonstrating the potential of soft robotics for safe and adaptive interactions across haptics, gripping, and medical applications. Bio: Amy Kyungwon Han is an Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering at Seoul National University. She was a postdoctoral researcher at Stanford and received a Ph.D. and M.S. from Stanford and a B.S. from Georgia Tech. Her research includes soft actuators, sensors, medical robotics, haptics, and manipulation. Prof. Han's awards include the MIT Technology Review Innovators Under 35 Asia Pacific, 50 Women in Robotics, Rising Star of RoboSoft, ICRA New Generation Star, and Best RA-L Paper Award. She serves as associate vice president of Technical Activities Board and as co-chair of Technical Committee on Haptics within IEEE Robotics and Automation Society.
event.title: Design and Application of Soft Robotics in Haptics, Gripping, and Medicine

event.description: 2026 Barbara Grosz Distinguished Lecture in AI and Society Title: AI's Models of the World, and Ours Speaker: Jon Kleinberg, Tisch University Professor in the Departments of Computer Science and Information Science at Cornell University Abstract: When we see someone performing at the top of their craft, we often marvel both at their observable achievements and the hidden, internal expertise that they've accumulated. Something similar is true with generative AI and large language models (LLMs): their successes involve both powerful observable behavior as well as deep internal representations of the world that they construct for their own uses. How do these internal representations work, and how similar or different are they compared to the representations of the world that we build as humans? This distinction is becoming crucial as people interact with powerful AI systems, where a mismatch between the system's model of the world and our human models of the world can lead to situations in which the system inadvertently `sets us up to fail' through our interactions with it. We explore these questions through the lens of generative AI, drawing on examples from game-playing, geographic navigation, and other complex tasks: When we train a model to win chess games, what happens when we pair it with a weaker partner who makes some of the moves? When we train a model to find shortest driving routes, what happens when it has to deal with unexpected detours? The picture we construct is further complicated by theoretical results indicating that successful generation can be achieved even by agents that are provably incapable of identifying the model they're generating from. The talk will include joint work with Ashton Anderson, Karim Hamade, Reid McIlroy-Young, Siddhartha Sen, Justin Chen, Sendhil Mullainathan, Ashesh Rambachan, Keyon Vafa, Fan Wei, Chris Qiu, and Prabhakar Raghavan.
